Nothing else is unnatural.

verdict.wording: FR: « mettre fin au contrat » does not say whose contract it is, whereas EN says 'a worker's employment' and AR says « إنهاء خدمته ». The meaning is still clear from context. « mettre fin au contrat de travail du salarié » would be more precise. « donner un préavis » is acceptable, but « notifier un préavis écrit » is more idiomatic in legal French. The place name « aux Émirats arabes unis » sits after « relations de travail », so it grammatically attaches to that phrase rather than to the decree-law. Writing « du décret-loi fédéral des Émirats arabes unis n° 33 de 2021 » would avoid this. AR: « بالأيام » in the middle of the question repeats « أجب بعدد الأيام » at the end. One of them can be dropped, preferably the one in the middle. A jurist would more naturally write « ما مدة الإخطار الكتابي التي يجب على صاحب العمل مراعاتها (أو: أن يُخطر بها العامل) », because the duration (المدة) is what the employer observes, not what he sends. As written, « الذي يجب ... أن يوجّهه » refers back to الإخطار, which is grammatical but slightly awkward after « ما مدة ».

verdict.wording: FR: in French law, 'congé parental' usually means the long, mostly unpaid 'congé parental d'éducation'. A French jurist may find 'congé parental payé' odd. It still correctly translates the UAE 'إجازة والدية', but 'congé parental (إجازة والدية)' would remove any doubt. 'Jours ouvrés' is correct for 'working days' / 'أيام عمل'. AR: 'ما عدد أيام العمل من الإجازة الوالدية مدفوعة الأجر التي يستحقها العامل' is correct but a little heavy. A more natural wording is 'كم يوم عمل من الإجازة الوالدية مدفوعة الأجر يستحق العامل…', or 'ما مدة الإجازة الوالدية مدفوعة الأجر، بأيام العمل، التي يستحقها العامل…'. All three versions say 'after the birth' and leave out the statute's time limit for taking the leave (within six months of the birth), but they leave it out in the same way, so the answer is not affected.

FR: 'avec et sans salaire confondus' is understandable but slightly loose; a French jurist would more naturally write 'rémunéré et non rémunéré confondus' or 'qu'il soit rémunéré ou non'. EN and AR read naturally, and the AR matches the official title and the law's own phrase 'بدون أجر'. One point applies to all three versions equally: the law has three tiers (full pay, half pay, unpaid), and 'with and without pay' does not name the half-pay tier. The word 'total' covers all of them, so the expected number is the same in every version.

verdict.wording: EN: 'the end-of-service gratuity is the basic wage of how many days?' reads badly. A native lawyer would write 'the end-of-service gratuity is calculated on the basis of how many days' basic wage?' or 'is equal to how many days' basic wage?'. AR: 'تُحتسب مكافأة نهاية الخدمة بأجر كم يومٍ من الأجر الأساسي' says 'wage' twice (أجر ... من الأجر الأساسي) and sounds clumsy. More natural: 'تُحتسب مكافأة نهاية الخدمة على أساس أجر كم يومًا من الأجر الأساسي' or simply 'تُحتسب مكافأة نهاية الخدمة بأجر كم يومًا أساسيًّا'. Small point: 'في دولة الإمارات العربية المتحدة' is not part of the decree-law's official title. It works as context, but placing it after the title, separated by a comma, would avoid suggesting it is part of the name. FR: no problem.

verdict.wording: FR: 'durée normale maximale du travail' is understandable but sounds a little forced. For a French labour lawyer, 'durée maximale' usually means the absolute ceiling including overtime, while 'durée normale/légale' means the threshold before overtime starts, so putting the two together is slightly unclear. 'Nombre maximal d'heures normales de travail par semaine' or 'durée maximale du travail normal hebdomadaire' would follow EN 'normal working hours' and AR 'ساعات العمل العادية' more closely. Also minor: 'aux Émirats arabes unis' comes right after the title, so it reads as part of it; 'décret-loi fédéral des Émirats arabes unis n° 33 de 2021' reads more naturally. EN and AR: no issues.

Minor, optional: in the FR version, 'aux Émirats arabes unis' sits after 'relations de travail', so it grammatically modifies the relations of employment rather than the decree-law. 'du décret-loi fédéral des Émirats arabes unis n° 33 de 2021 relatif à la réglementation des relations de travail' would mirror the EN more closely. The meaning is not affected, and the AR places 'في دولة الإمارات العربية المتحدة' in the same position. 'Sur la réglementation' is also a common rendering of 'بشأن', but 'relatif à' is correct. The AR matches the official title and the statutory verb 'تشغيل'. The EN is natural.

FR: « combien d'années après la fin de la relation de travail une action … n'est-elle plus recevable ? » is grammatical but heavy. A French jurist would more naturally write « au bout de combien d'années à compter de la fin de la relation de travail une action … devient-elle irrecevable ? » or « … se heurte-t-elle à une fin de non-recevoir ? ». AR: the sentence « ما المدة التي لا تُسمع بعد مضيّها، من تاريخ انتهاء علاقة العمل، الدعوى … » is awkward because the subject الدعوى comes last and the phrase between commas breaks it up. A smoother version that follows the statute: « ما المدة التي لا تُسمع الدعوى المتعلقة بأيٍّ من الحقوق المقرّرة في هذا المرسوم بقانون بعد مضيّها من تاريخ انتهاء علاقة العمل؟ ». EN: the official English title uses "Regulation of Labour Relations". "employment relations" is acceptable but not the official title. "a claim for rights under this decree-law" could be closer to the Arabic "any of the rights" (أيٍّ من الحقوق), for example "a claim relating to any of the rights established by this decree-law". This is a style point only: the meaning is the same.

1) EN: the official English title of the law is 'Federal Decree by Law No. 33 of 2021 Regarding the Regulation of Labour Relations'. 'On the regulation of employment relations' is understandable, but 'Labour Relations' would match the official title. 2) The 'final decision' wording is slightly off in all three languages, and differently in each. The amended Article 54 makes the Ministry's decision binding and enforceable, with the force of an executive instrument (سند تنفيذي), but a party can still challenge it before the court. In Arabic, 'قرار نهائي' suggests a decision that cannot be appealed. In French, 'décision définitive' is ambiguous: it can mean a decision that settles the merits but can still be appealed, or a decision with no further appeal ('en dernier ressort'). The English 'final' falls between the two. This does not change the expected number. Still, a native jurist would find wording closer to the law more natural: AR 'بقرار ملزم / له قوة السند التنفيذي', FR 'par une décision exécutoire', EN 'by a binding decision'. 3) AR: the law itself uses the plural 'المنازعات العمالية الفردية'. 'المنازعة العمالية الفردية' would follow the legal text more closely than 'النزاع العمالي الفردي', though the current phrase is acceptable.

AR: 'للعمال والموظفين' is a weak rendering of 'ouvriers et employés'. In Arabic legal usage 'الموظفين' usually means public servants or civil-service staff, and 'العمال' means workers in general rather than manual workers. The French gloss in brackets prevents a real change in meaning, but a native jurist would prefer 'العمال اليدويين والمستخدمين' (or 'العمال والمستخدمين'). AR: 'عقد العمل غير محدد المدة' is acceptable, but 'عقد العمل لمدة غير محددة' is the more usual legal phrasing. EN: 'permanent contract' is common usage; 'open-ended (indefinite-term) contract' would be more precise for a CDI.

verdict.wording: EN and AR define jours ouvrables as all days except the weekly rest day and public holidays. FR gives no definition. This changes nothing in meaning, but the definition is slightly loose: jours ouvrables exclude only public holidays that are normally not worked (jours fériés chômés), not every public holiday. EN: the gloss would read more precisely as 'all days except the weekly rest day and public holidays not normally worked'. AR: 'الأيام المفتوحة للعمل' is an unnatural calque; most Arabic legal texts use 'أيام العمل' (with jours ouvrables in brackets to keep it apart from jours ouvrés). The repeated 'كم يومًا من الأيام ... من العطلة' is clumsy; 'كم يومَ عمل (jours ouvrables ...) من العطلة السنوية المدفوعة الأجر' reads better. 'العطل الرسمية' would be more exact as 'أيام العطل الرسمية غير المعمول بها'. FR: no issues.
